analysis.summary: This is technically adjacent to METSS Corporation's advanced-materials, formulation, testing, validation, product-development, pilot-scale, and light-manufacturing capabilities, but it is not a general applied-materials opportunity. It requires a mature, FDA-regulated medical-device program with both a milestone-driven translational UG3 phase and a clinical UH3 phase. The approved METSS profile does not establish that METSS owns such a device or can independently satisfy the medical-device regulatory, clinical, human-subjects, and patient-care requirements. METSS therefore has an evidence-backed potential subcontractor or technical-development-partner role—such as device-materials development, materials compatibility, bench/performance testing, packaging-related development, or scale-up—but no evidence-backed basis to prime independently. Listed receipt dates extend through January 28, 2028, but the reviewed material also states a January 29, 2028 expiration date; the active NOFO and next usable receipt cycle must be verified before planning submission.
analysis.immediate_action: Do not initiate a standalone METSS application. First identify a device-owner/clinical lead with a near-final FDA-regulated device and confirm participating-IC mission fit. Obtain a defined METSS work package tied to UG3/UH3 milestones—preferably materials, compatibility, verification/validation, packaging, or manufacturing-scale-up work—then verify METSS registrations and proposal capacity. Contact the NIH Scientific/Research Contact before committing; the announcement recommends contact preferably at least 12 weeks before a receipt date and requires contact at least 6 weeks before a receipt date for requests of $500,000 or more in direct costs in any year. Confirm the currently active deadline because of the stated expiration/last-cycle inconsistency.
caveats: This assessment uses only the official Grants.gov record, the supplied document-review findings, and the approved METSS public profile.

deepAccepted.title: US Army Combat Capabilities Development Command Broad Agency Announcement
deepAccepted.summary: This is a technically relevant Army Soldier Center BAA for METSS, particularly in chemical/biological protection, CBRN decontamination and survivability, protective and EMI-related materials, functional fluids, testing, and applied R&D transition/scale-up. The Official Grants.gov record expressly permits commercial firms, which conditionally supports METSS organizational eligibility. However, the available SAM.gov review contains only a webpage shell and does not provide the actual solicitation, active topics, required proposal content, mandatory registrations, restrictions, or evaluation criteria. Accordingly, METSS has evidence-backed technical relevance but not enough evidence for a responsible pursue decision or a defined prime/subcontract role. The Grants.gov record lists a response date of February 27, 2030, but current topic acceptance and solicitation status remain unverified.

analysis.summary: PAR-25-053 is technically adjacent rather than a direct strategic fit for METSS Corporation. METSS has credible public evidence for a meaningful subcontract or research-partner work package in device materials, coatings/polymers, material compatibility, non-clinical characterization, verification/validation support, and selected process-development or pilot-scale activities. The opportunity, however, is specifically for mature low-risk neural therapeutic or diagnostic devices progressing through a required NSR clinical-study phase. METSS's approved public profile does not establish a neural-device asset, neurological indication, clinical team, FDA/IRB pathway, clinical-trial capability, or required registrations. Accordingly, METSS should investigate only as a scoped non-clinical research partner to an established device and clinical lead, not as a standalone prime based on currently approved public evidence. The final listed submission date is January 28, 2027; earlier listed cycles have passed relative to the current 2026 profile version, subject to confirmation of the live opportunity status and current NIH instructions.
analysis.immediate_action: Conduct a targeted partner screen immediately: identify an eligible neural-device developer or academic/clinical lead with a near-final low-risk device and NSR clinical-study plan, then request a defined R61 work package for METSS covering materials selection/formulation, compatibility, environmental or performance testing, verification/validation support, or process scale-up. In parallel, obtain internal verification of SAM/UEI, Grants.gov, eRA Commons, PD/PI availability, capacity, IP position, and willingness to participate. If no partner has an evidence-supported neurological-device program, representative entry data, and viable NSR clinical path, close the opportunity as not actionable.

analysis.summary: PAR-25-336 is strategically adjacent to METSS's applied materials, chemistry, analytical characterization, testing, and process-scale-up capabilities, but the public METSS profile does not establish the core TTNCI requirement: an advanced-preclinical engineered cancer nanoparticle or nano-device with a defined oncology objective and supporting preliminary evidence. METSS therefore has a potentially meaningful supporting research work package—such as formulation/material development, physicochemical characterization, compatibility/performance testing, or process optimization—but no evidence-backed basis to prime this R01 independently. Eligibility is conditional rather than established because NIH registrations, qualified PD/PI/Signing Official arrangements, clinical expertise, and animal-study resources remain unverified. The appropriate posture is targeted investigation for a collaborator-led application, not immediate proposal commitment.
analysis.immediate_action: Within a short qualification call, determine whether METSS or an external technology owner has a specific engineered cancer nanomedicine/nano-device at or below 300 nm, a defined tumor indication, and qualifying advanced-preclinical data. If yes, identify an oncology clinical lead and animal-study partner, define METSS's bounded formulation/characterization/process-development work package, and verify NIH/SAM/eRA registration readiness before selecting an available listed submission cycle. If no such intervention and evidence package exist, close the opportunity as nonresponsive for METSS.
caveats: The official record lists scheduled new-application due dates through November 15, 2027, including May 17, 2027 and November 15, 2027; the supplied materials do not prove which cycle is currently open relative to the intended submission date. Verify current NIH/Grants.gov status before committing resources.

analysis.summary: PAR-25-325 is technically adjacent to METSS only through its broad analytical and testing capabilities. Its core requirement is cancer-focused clinical biospecimen science and clinical assay analytical validation, supported by clinical sample access, biomarker/assay expertise, human-subjects infrastructure, and multidisciplinary clinical leadership. Those requirements are not evidenced in the approved METSS public profile. A materials-centered response may also be nonresponsive because the NOFO excludes novel biospecimen fixative or technology-development projects. METSS is not shown to be legally ineligible as a for-profit organization, but mandatory registrations and program-specific execution requirements remain unknown. No meaningful, evidence-backed METSS work package is currently established; therefore METSS should not pursue this opportunity based on the available record.

analysis.summary: PAR-25-353 is an open, recurring NIH/NIMH U19 opportunity for integrated, multidisciplinary discovery and early development programs addressing mental disorders, SUDs, or AUD. METSS has broad applied-R&D capabilities that could be relevant only at the margin to a specifically defined therapeutic-device materials, formulation, or validation task. The approved public profile does not establish a disease-area research program, a novel psychiatric therapeutic or neurotechnology concept, an eligible NIH program team, clinical-development capability, or required submission readiness. Therefore, there is no evidence-backed meaningful METSS work package or role at this time, despite conditional organizational eligibility as a domestic for-profit entity.
analysis.immediate_action: Do not allocate proposal-development resources or pursue as prime or subcontractor. analysis.summary: This is a strategically relevant but highly open-ended NSWC Crane long-range BAA. METSS has evidence-backed potential contributions in advanced materials, protective/barrier materials, specialty chemistry and functional fluids, harsh-environment formulation and validation, process development, pilot-scale scale-up, and testing. However, the reviewed opportunity does not identify a current materials- or chemistry-specific requirement, funding line, or defined work package. METSS should not commit to proposal development until it identifies a differentiated concept tied to a named Crane technical capability and obtains technical-POC confirmation that the concept is current, nonduplicative, and fundable. analysis.immediate_action: Develop a one- to five-page, nonproprietary concept outline centered on a specific METSS-led technical work package—for example, harsh-environment material, protective/barrier material, specialty fluid, signature-management material, power-system material, or validation method—then contact the relevant NSWC Crane technical POC to confirm fit, current funding interest, principal/adjunct technical capability, nonduplication, security posture, and preferred submission path before preparing the required white paper. analysis.summary: This is a strategically strong technical match for METSS’s applied-research identity in CBRN protection/decontamination, advanced polymers and barrier materials, specialty chemistry, and validation under harsh conditions. The strongest historical topic alignments were Amendment 2 B4 (PFAS-free omniphobic protective materials) and B6 (cross-linked polymer detection films), supported by both official topic scope and METSS public materials, chemistry, testing, and CBRN evidence. However, B1–B6 closed on March 2, 2026, and the supplied record does not establish an extension. METSS therefore should not treat the expired topics as available. A general-thrust Phase I submission may remain possible under the continuing BAA through September 30, 2034, but only after DTRA technical pre-coordination and confirmation of a viable funding path. METSS has an evidence-backed potential prime role for a materials/protection/decontamination-focused fundamental-research concept, but prime eligibility remains conditional on administrative and proposal-specific requirements.
analysis.immediate_action: Within the next business day, contact the listed DTRA BAA mailbox to confirm whether a general-thrust white paper is currently being accepted, identify the appropriate technical point of contact, and ask whether any B4/B6 successor, reopened topic, or related active call exists. In parallel, internally verify METSS SAM/UEI/Grants.gov status and decide whether to develop a university-supported, broadly publishable general-thrust concept focused on PFAS-free chemical-protective materials, agent/decontaminant compatibility, or fundamental polymer-film protection/detection mechanisms.

deepAccepted.title: TTO Office Wide (OW) BAA 2025
deepAccepted.type: Cooperative Agreement / Grant / Other / Procurement Contract
deepAccepted.summary: This is a strategically relevant broad DARPA BAA with plausible METSS work-package fit in advanced materials, specialty chemistry/functional fluids, test and validation, and manufacturing scale-up. METSS's public profile supports an initial investigation because TTO explicitly values manufacturability, production responsiveness, supply-chain alternatives, and accelerated testing. deepAccepted.title: Chemical Process Systems (CPS)
deepAccepted.summary: CPS is technically relevant to METSS's applied chemistry, functional fluids, advanced materials, analytical testing, process development, pilot-scale operations, and manufacturing-scale-up identity. METSS has a potentially meaningful technical role in translating fundamental process concepts into formulations, materials, experimental validation, durability/compatibility testing, and scale-up-oriented process design. However, CPS is explicitly a fundamental-research NSF program, and the approved profile does not establish the registrations, organizational eligibility, personnel availability, NSF proposal readiness, or academic research structure needed for a submission. The strongest current path is to investigate a university-led collaboration or a METSS-led submission only after eligibility and research-lead requirements are verified. This is not yet an evidence-backed pursue decision.
deepAccepted.why: CPS supports fundamental chemical-process research spanning reaction engineering, thermodynamics, reactor and process design, catalysis, electrochemical systems, separations, polymers, chemicals, fuels, waste reduction, and molecular-to-process/plant-scale integration.: The reviewed CPS program description identifies these as core technical areas and applications of the CPS program. (NSF Program Desccription PD-26-367Y) METSS has a credible potential work package in chemistry, formulation and process development, analytical characterization, materials/process testing, and scale-up-oriented process engineering.: METSS publicly lists physical, organic, inorganic, and analytical chemistry; sample analysis, reaction characterization, formulation, and product development; mechanical and chemical engineering; product and process design from laboratory development through commercial production; pilot-scale operations; and advanced analytical and materials-compatibility testing. (Approved METSS public profile) METSS materials and polymer capabilities align with CPS interest in process and materials innovation, including polymer processing and scalable chemical-process technologies.: METSS publicly lists polymers, composite resins, coatings, adhesives, specialty resins, packaging and barrier films, polymer processing and recycling, and materials for harsh chemical environments. (Approved METSS public profile) METSS has public past-performance examples relevant to applied chemical-process and materials-development work, though they do not by themselves demonstrate NSF fundamental-research proposal readiness.: The profile lists DPA Title III Critical Chemicals Production, Critical Supply Chain Production of Energetic Materials and Associated Precursors, Lubricating Oil Study, Non-PFAS Elastomeric Chemical Barrier Materials, and other applied R&D contracts. (Approved METSS public profile)

deepAccepted.summary: This is a technically relevant broad NIST research vehicle, with the strongest apparent METSS path in MML-aligned materials, chemical, biological, or biomolecular measurement research. METSS’s public advanced-materials, specialty-chemistry, analytical, validation, and CBRN-testing capabilities support a meaningful potential work package, and its public past performance reinforces applied research credibility. Nevertheless, the opportunity is not yet a clear pursue decision because the NOFO requires alignment to a specific component and current division-level objective, while the supplied materials do not confirm an active METSS-relevant topic or funding capacity. METSS is eligible in principle as a for-profit non-Federal entity, but formal submission eligibility and operational readiness remain conditional on unverified registrations and proposal-specific requirements. The appropriate role is conditional prime applicant for a narrowly scoped research project, not a commercialization or product-development proposal.

analysis.summary: METSS has moderate technical adjacency to possible Genesis Mission materials, manufacturing, chemistry, critical-materials, and energy-fluid workflows through its documented applied R&D, testing, analytical, formulation, and scale-up capabilities. However, the opportunity is fundamentally for interdisciplinary teams demonstrating novel AI-enabled R&D workflows and measurable AI advantage. The approved public profile does not establish METSS AI capability, a responsive AI work package, required team composition, or applicant-specific compliance and cost-share readiness. More importantly, the FY26 Phase I and direct Phase II deadlines have passed, while the remaining FY26 Phase II deadline is available only to Phase I recipients—a status not established for METSS. Therefore, METSS should not pursue this posting as an active opportunity.

analysis.summary: This is technically relevant only as a partner-led, field-deployment opportunity, with Topic Area 2 presenting the most credible path. METSS's documented chemistry, advanced-materials, process-development, analytical, compatibility-testing, pilot-scale, and validation capabilities could form a meaningful work package for treatment-material evaluation, fouling/corrosion and compatibility studies, analytical characterization, process optimization, and field-performance validation. However, the public record does not show that METSS has a produced-water treatment technology, qualifying field site/feedstock, oil-and-gas operator access, or high-throughput long-duration operating capability. Topic Areas 1a–1c lack a sufficiently evidenced METSS technical work package. Pursue only through a qualified industry-led Topic Area 2 team after rapid diligence; METSS should not presently position itself as prime based on the approved public profile.
analysis.immediate_action: Before committing bid resources, contact qualified U.S. produced-water operators/treatment integrators to determine whether a Topic Area 2 field project has a defined TRL-5-or-higher technology, a 15,000–50,000 barrel/day U.S. site, more-than-one-year operating plan, and a signer for the required industry intent letter. In parallel, conduct internal eligibility diligence on domestic ownership/control, SAM/UEI/eXCHANGE status, exclusions, research-security disclosures, cost-share capacity, available staff/equipment, and whether METSS will accept a research-partner role. If these conditions cannot be confirmed promptly, do not submit for the September 8, 2026 deadline.

analysis.summary: This is a strategically relevant, continuously open ARL foundational-research BAA with broad eligibility that can potentially accommodate METSS applied R&D in advanced materials, functional fluids, chemical/biological survivability, validation, and scale-up. METSS's public profile supports a plausible role in a materials- or chemistry-centered topic, potentially as a prime or technical subcontractor depending on the live topic and team. However, the official live topic portal was not substantively available in the reviewed source set, and the historical topic snapshots cannot prove that a matching topic remains active. Accordingly, there is no evidence-backed current work package, no basis to select prime versus subcontractor, and no basis to finalize eligibility beyond conditional base-BAA eligibility. The proper disposition is investigate rather than pursue immediately.
analysis.immediate_action: Retrieve and preserve the current live ARL BAA topic record(s), including topic ID, status, TPOC, due/preferred submission timing, award instrument, and special requirements. analysis.summary: ECLIPSE is strategically adjacent to METSS's applied materials, chemistry, characterization, testing, and scale-up profile, especially for a plasma-surface-interaction, plasma-enabled coating/materials, plasma chemical-measurement, or plasma-enabled environmental-remediation concept. However, this is not a strong METSS standalone pursuit: the official program requires a fundamental plasma-science/engineering challenge, while METSS's approved public profile provides no plasma-specific technical capability or past-performance evidence. METSS has a plausible, meaningful research-partner role supporting materials formulation and response, analytical characterization, compatibility/performance testing, and transition-oriented validation under a plasma-science-led team. The relevant deadline is controlled by the receiving NSF program. Supplied ECLIPSE materials list windows through September 29, 2026 for several participating programs, September 1–30, 2026 for CHE CSDM-B, October/November 2026 windows for certain programs, and November 16, 2026 for PHY Plasma Physics; the receiving-program page must control because one CHE date is internally inconsistent.

analysis.summary: This is a low-strength opportunity for METSS as a prime but may warrant limited partner outreach. The required work concerns sustainable global fungal-disease detection, diagnosis, surveillance, workforce development, data use, and public-health response—not materials development or general applied research. METSS has adjacent BSL-2 and analytical/testing capabilities that could support a narrowly defined laboratory-capacity or validation work package, but its public profile does not establish fungal-disease expertise, global public-health implementation capacity, country partnerships, or the primary-recipient management infrastructure required by the NOFO. METSS should not lead an application based on the available evidence. The official Grants.gov record lists a September 30, 2026 closing date, while the Info Session lists August 31, 2026; the live package and CDC must confirm the controlling deadline. Expected award timing also conflicts: the NOFO indicates December 2026 award/January 2027 start, while the slides indicate September 30, 2026 anticipated award.
analysis.immediate_action: Verify the live Grants.gov deadline and application status immediately. In parallel, conduct a short partner screen limited to established global-health/fungal-disease prime candidates. Proceed only if a qualified prime can identify a specific allowable, non-research METSS testing or laboratory-capacity work package and METSS internally verifies registrations, availability, pricing, and willingness to participate. Do not commit to a prime submission on the present record.

analysis.summary: This opportunity is strategically adjacent to METSS's documented CBRN, chemistry, formulation, materials, and testing identity, but it is an MCM-development NOFO rather than a decontamination, chemical-agent-persistence, survivability, or generic chemical-testing solicitation. The approved METSS profile does not establish a candidate medical countermeasure, medically relevant efficacy program, required preliminary data, or a distinct and permitted technical work package. The strongest documented CBRN activities risk falling within Area 4 exclusions for environmental decontamination or analytical/diagnostic work. Although for-profit organizations may apply, METSS's required NIH and Federal registrations are unverified. Therefore, METSS should not pursue as prime or subcontractor on the available evidence.
